formula: fte ~ post * state + (1 | store)
notes: ch5 do-file: xtset store post; treated = state*post; xtreg fte post treated, fe (Card & Krueger minimum-wage DiD). Fixed-effects panel rendered with a store random intercept (#22 convention); treated is the post:state interaction, stores nested in state. Hand pass #82: chapter 5 fits store fixed effects and does not establish the store random intercept; the formula stays an inferred candidate.

formula: attain ~ p7vrq + p7read + dadocc + dadunemp + daded + momed + male + deprive + (1 | neighid) + (1 | schid)
notes: Scottish cross-classified neighbourhood-and-school data (Garner & Raudenbush); pupils cross-classified by neighbourhood (neighid) and school (schid), educational attainment the outcome. Recalled the cross-classified model. dummy ignored. Hand pass #82: exercise 9.5(4) fits this Gaussian model with crossed neighborhood and school intercepts.

formula: program ~ I(pcountry == jcountry) + (1 | pair) + (1 | judge)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: figure-skating scores cross-classified by skating pair and judge; technical score (performance) the outcome, program the artistic score (alternate response, ignored), pcountry/jcountry the nationalities behind the nationalistic-bias question. Labels sparse. Hand pass #82: exercise 9.7 models the program score with a same-country indicator in place of additive nationality effects; the raw pcountry and jcountry stay the covariates.

formula: luclms ~ ez + year + (1 | city)
notes: Enterprise-zone difference-in-differences panel (Papke): city observed in two years (1983/1984), log unemployment claims (luclms) the outcome, ez the enterprise-zone indicator. Panel grouped by city. Hand pass #82: exercise 5.3 fits city fixed effects; with two years, numeric and factor year span the same fixed effects, and the city random intercept stays an adaptation.

formula: pat ~ logr + logr1 + logr2 + logr3 + logr4 + logr5 + factor(year) + logk + scisect + (1 | cusip)
notes: Hausman-Hall-Griliches patents-R&D count panel; firm (cusip) observed over years, patent counts (pat) the outcome, log R&D (logr) and log capital (logk) covariates. Lagged pat1-pat4 and logr1-logr5 ignored. Recalled the Poisson panel. Hand pass #82: exercise 13.4(3) fits this Poisson model; the lag columns hold values before the observed panel and stay separate inputs.

formula: pass_read ~ female + isei + high_school + college + one_for + both_for + test_lang + (1 | schoolid)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: PISA 2000 USA reading, students in schools (schoolid); passing reading proficiency (pass_read) the outcome, socio-economic index (isei) and background covariates. Survey weights (w_fstuwt, wnrschbw) and variance strata ignored. female is a category dtype. Hand pass #82: exercise 10.8(1) fits this Bernoulli-logit model; its id_school and schoolid identify the same groups.

formula: lme4::glmer(stops ~ factor(eth, levels=c(3,1,2)) + prblack + prhisp + offset(log(arrests)) + (1 + factor(eth, levels=c(3,1,2)) | precinct), family=poisson(link="log"), data=subset(police, crime == 1))
notes: NYC stop-and-frisk data (Gelman, ARM ch.15): stop counts by precinct, ethnicity (eth) and crime type (crime), offset by log arrests. Recalled the ARM Poisson multilevel model. precinct the grouping; arrests the offset. Hand pass #82: the final source fit has correlated ethnicity coefficients by precinct, white the reference, on crime 1 only; crime selects the rows and arrests is the exposure.

formula: w ~ sex + factor(dose) + I(ave(w, dam, FUN=function(z) sum(!is.na(z)))) + (1 | dam)
notes: Rat-pups teratology data (West et al.): pups (rat) nested in litters (dam), birth weight (w) the outcome, dose the treatment applied to the dam, sex a pup covariate. Recalled the litter random-intercept model. Hand pass #82: exercise 3.4 adds litter size, derived in the formula only. Kept apart from nlme RatPupWeight: that table has an extra female pup in litter 11, and two weights differ (here/nlme 5.72/5.75 for a litter-14 male, 5.39/5.93 for a litter-27 female); which is right is unresolved.

formula: kscore ~ arm + factor(sex) + factor(scpar) + (1 | school)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: SHARE school-based sex-education cluster RCT, pupils in 25 schools (school); onset of sexual activity (debut, 0/1) the primary outcome, arm the randomised intervention, scpar social class. kscore (knowledge) and regret are alternate/subset outcomes (ignored). Hand pass #82: exercise 3.8 models the signed knowledge score with Gaussian errors; its negative values rule out a count or binomial reading.

formula: birwt ~ smoke + male + mage + hsgrad + somecoll + collgrad + married + black + kessner2 + kessner3 + novisit + pretri2 + pretri3 + (1 | momid)
notes: ch3 do-file: mixed birwt smoke male mage hsgrad somecoll collgrad married black kessner2 kessner3 novisit pretri2 pretri3 || momid: (mother random intercept). Abrevaya sibling birth-weight/smoking panel; smoke/male/black are category dtypes, magesq = mage^2, cigs/gestat alternate measures (ignored).

formula: lme4::lmer(tmaths ~ factor(classt) + (1 | schid) + (1 | schid:class), data=subset(star1, grade == 0), REML=FALSE)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Project STAR class-size experiment; students in classes (class = school*teacher*grade) in schools (schid), reading score (treads) the outcome, class type (classt) the treatment. Large merged file; tmaths an alternate response, race/weight columns ignored. RULE GAP: student (stdntid) repeats across grades, so a pupil random effect is also defensible. Hand pass #82: exercise 8.6(5) models kindergarten mathematics scores with school and class intercepts; the kindergarten restriction removes the repeated-grade ambiguity.

formula: log1p(tax) ~ log(tpi) + prep + ms + hh + depend + age + mr + emp + (1 | subject)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: panel of tax filers, subject observed over time; log tax (lntax) the outcome, log income (lntpi) and prep (used a preparer) covariates. tpi/tax the raw levels of the logged columns (ignored). Labels uninformative. Hand pass #82: exercise 5.1 fits this model, mr included; the deposited values give lntax = log(tax + 1), zero taxes included, and lntpi = log(tpi). The raw tax stays the continuous response.

formula: dtlm ~ level * factor(group) + (1 | famnum) + (1 | famnum:id)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Tower of London cognitive task (Rabe-Hesketh, Skrondal & Pickles): subjects (id) within families (famnum) measured at task levels (level, -1/0/1); tlm the Tower-of-London measure. Alternate measures (tlpl, tlsub, dtlm) ignored, group the family-type. RULE GAP: several correlated measures per occasion; filed tlm as the response. Hand pass #82: exercise 16.2(4) fits a binary logit of task performance with difficulty-by-diagnostic-group interactions and family and person intercepts.

formula: lme4::lmer(y ~ 1 + (1 | rater) + (1 | video), data=subset(videos, novice == 1), REML=TRUE)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: ratings of videos cross-classified by rater and video; y the rating (count, 0-19), novice whether the rater is a novice. Cross-classified random effects. No labels. Hand pass #82: exercise 9.4 fits novice raters only, so novice selects the rows instead of entering the mean. The 0-22 score stays a count under the Gaussian likelihood; what it counts is undocumented.

formula: lwage ~ black + hisp + union + married + exper + I(year - 1980) + I(educ - 12) + (1 + exper | nr)
notes: ch5/ch6 do-file: mixed lwage black hisp union married exper yeart educt || nr: exper, covariance(unstructured) (random intercept and exper slope). Wooldridge wage panel, 545 men over 1980-1987 (nr); yeart/educt the year-trend and schooling terms, rendered year/educ. Occupation/industry dummies, d81-d87 and expersq ignored. Hand pass #82: the formula records the source centering, year at 1980 and educ at 12.

formula: wemp ~ husunemp + under1 + under5 + age + (1 | case)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: women's employment panel, woman (case) observed over time; employment (wemp, 0/1) the outcome, husband's unemployment (husunemp) and young-children indicators (under1, under5) covariates. No labels. Hand pass #82: the exact fit was not found in the chapter or exercise scripts; published status unverified.

formula: y ~ smoking + age + (1 | id)
notes: Steubenville childhood wheeze longitudinal data: children (id) measured repeatedly (var the occasion, age centred), wheeze (y, 0/1) the outcome, maternal smoking (smoking) the covariate. Recalled the subject random-intercept logit. Hand pass #82: exercise 10.2(2) fits this random-intercept logit.

formula: lwage ~ exp + I(exp^2) + wks + occ + ind + south + smsa + ms + union + ed + fem + blk + (1 | nr)
notes: Cornwell-Rupert returns-to-schooling panel; 595 individuals (nr) over 7 years, log wage (lwage) the outcome, experience/weeks-worked/union/schooling covariates. Panel grouped by nr. Recalled the random-effects wage model. Hand pass #82: exercise 5.7's random-effects model adds squared experience.

formula: yield ~ moist + (1 | variety)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: wheat variety trial, 10 varieties each grown on 6 plots; yield the outcome modelled with a variety random intercept, moist a moisture covariate, plot the replicate index. #24 cluster rule: variety repeats within the table and indexes the grouping. No labels. VERDICT 2026-10-08: the six plots are the blocks each of the ten varieties is grown in; block random, variety fixed, as leafblotch in #23 (blind reading). Hand pass #82: exercise 4.4's final fit, used for prediction, has a variety intercept and no slope; the 2026-10-08 fixed-variety, random-block reading is overturned.

formula: y ~ price + contract + local + known + tod + seasonal + (0 + price + contract + local + known + tod + seasonal | id)
notes: Read help (no labels); no do-file model. Stated-preference electricity-supplier choice, choice tasks (experiment) per respondent (id); y the chosen option. Model inferred. SPOT CHECK (Alex, 2026-10-08): a mixed discrete-choice model with respondent-specific random coefficients on the six attributes, id the chooser; formula rewritten. Hand pass #82: refused as a choice model: each experiment holds four mutually exclusive alternatives, and the final source fit is a mixed logit with correlated respondent coefficients on local and known only.

formula: log(uclms) ~ ez + factor(year) + (1 | city)
notes: Read help labels (uclms unemployment claims, ez enterprise zone); ezunem not in a do-file model. Enterprise-zone unemployment panel, city over year (1980-88). uclms modelled log-linearly (luclms); grouped by city. Year dummies, city dummies, lags and change columns in ignore. Model inferred. SPOT CHECK (Alex, 2026-10-08): the modelled outcome is log(uclms) with year effects; the raw column stays the response under the transform rule. Hand pass #82: exercise 7.8 fits a Gaussian model to the log of the positive integer claims; its separate year means equal the intercept plus year factor.
